Fuck that noise. microSD is the most fickle flash storage I have ever used in my life. I've probably got 4 of them in various sizes in brands in various states of corruption right now. They always seem to get worse the bigger they get, too.

Still pretty sweet that we've got 200GB in something the size of your pinkie nail. If you went back to the 1960's and showed them this their brains would implode.

Are there any technical reasons why microSD is substantially less reliable than, say, full SDXC or SDHC, CF or USB flash drives? IIRC USB flash storage offers up to something like 100,000 rewrites. Does the fact that microSD utilizes more bleeding-edge technology in terms of less-proven manufacturing or engineering methods have more to do with it than any other likely reason? Or is there some other limitation that microSD has as opposed to other storage media that makes it more prone to corruption?
I'm not sure, I personally haven't had problems. And I used to test equipment with SD/Micro SD cards.

I can't really weigh in on this too much because my opinion on microSD is based off of my own anecdotal experience. I don't know what it is about microSD that makes them seem more prone to corruption for me, but I would imagine it has something to do with the size. Almost all flash memory is a ticking time bomb, and even new chips are often riddled with bad sectors or corruption, which is why every SD card you buy is equipped with a microprocessor that helps to compensate for all of the bad sectors with complex algorithms. Hell, half the time, the flash chip inside your SD card was ripped out of some other device before it ever became an SD card. They recycle a lot of flash memory, which helps to further contribute to things like corruption when the algorithms can no longer do their job well enough. If you've ever seen the inside of a microSD, it's actually pretty neat. They're basically just a PCB with a flash chip and a bunch of traces. Easy to see how this might lead to some problems.

So basically, just based on nothing but opinion. I would say if there is a spike in corruption with microSD, it probably has to do with the limitations of size and the fickle nature of flash itself.
